Method of Attack: Infostealer malware infecting developers via npm package
Remote access trojan (RAT) capabilities including recording audio and phone calls, taking photos, reviewing browser history, accessing WhatsApp messages

Stealing instant messenger messages and databases, browser bookmarks and search history, files with specific extensions, clipboard data, notifications content, images, videos, SMS messages, phone contacts, call logs, GPS location, device information
Uses Accessibility Services or root access to harvest data
Triggered by Android contentObserver and Broadcast receivers on new contacts, messages, or app installs
Uses Firebase messaging service for command and control
Displays fake system update notifications to camouflage activity
Exfiltrates only recent data and thumbnails to reduce bandwidth and avoid detection
Attack Vector: Installed as 'System Update' app via third-party Android app stores
Requires user to enable Accessibility Services or root access
Triggered by system events like new contacts, messages, or app installs
Indicators of Compromise: Dedicated C&C server collecting stolen data via POST requests
Malware sample hashes and C2 server addresses available in Zimperium's report
